payload.reason: The evidence supports the hypothesis that humans' robustness to noise is due to their ability to utilize general knowledge, as it contrasts with MRC models that rely solely on specific passage-question pairs.

claims.text: Humans' robustness to noise is attributed to their ability to utilize general knowledge, unlike MRC models that depend on specific data.
The integration of general knowledge into MRC models enhances their robustness to noise, indicating the importance of general knowledge in reading comprehension.
The performance of the Knowledge Aided Reader (KAR) model, which uses general knowledge, demonstrates improved robustness to noise compared to traditional MRC models.
